input.note:
**Root Cause:** The platform-base v2 Helm chart (`platform-base-2.0.3`) introduced `automountServiceAccountToken: false` as a security hardening default. This prevents Kubernetes from mounting the ServiceAccount token at `/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token`. The `job-dispatcher` application requires this token to authenticate against the Kubernetes API (it uses in-cluster configuration), so it crashes immediately on startup.

**Evidence:**
- The crashing pod (`job-dispatcher-7b6f9c4d8-zk5np`) has `automountServiceAccountToken: false` and only one volume mount (`/tmp`) — no service account token volume present.
- The healthy old pod (`job-dispatcher-5d8b7c9f6d-q7m2x`, running `platform-base-1.8.0`) has the `kube-api-access-7xq2d` projected volume correctly mounted at `/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount`.
- Pod logs confirm the exact failure: `FATAL unable to load in-cluster configuration: open /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token: no such file or directory`

**Why it crashes:** When `automountServiceAccountToken: false` is set on a Pod spec, Kubernetes does not inject the credential volume, so any application relying on the standard in-cluster config path fails to start [cite: tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account#opt-out-of-api-credential-automounting-0]. The `automountServiceAccountToken` should only be `false` for pods that do not need access to the Kubernetes API [cite: concepts/security/application-security-checklist#service-account-0].

**Fix:** In your `job-dispatcher` Helm chart values, explicitly override the new chart default by setting `automountServiceAccountToken: true`. The Pod spec value takes precedence over both the chart default and the ServiceAccount-level setting [cite: tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-service-account#opt-out-of-api-credential-automounting-1], so this will restore the token mount without changing the platform-base chart itself. For example:

```yaml
# job-dispatcher values.yaml
automountServiceAccountToken: true
```

Once the Deployment is updated with this value, the rollout will complete and the new pod will be able to authenticate to the Kubernetes API successfully.
